description: Single-panel scatter plot with a drawn-through curve, titled "WHR(1.5%-1%) - Al content". The ordinate is "Work Hardening Rate (GPa)" spanning 0 to 20 with major ticks every 5 GPa; the abscissa is "Aluminium content (%)" spanning 0 to about 42 with major ticks every 10%. Two data sets are distinguished: filled circles joined by a solid black line, labelled "Binary Fe-Al", and two filled squares labelled "Fe-Al-B" that are connected to the main trend by a dashed line with arrowheads pointing to both squares. The Binary Fe-Al curve is low (<2 GPa) up to about 20% Al, rises steeply from ~20% Al, reaches its single highest point immediately above the 15 GPa gridline near the 30% Al tick, then falls back through the 10 GPa line at ~32% Al and flattens to just above 5 GPa at 40% Al. Scattered individual circles deviate from the joined trend at 20-29% Al. The two Fe-Al-B squares sit at ~20% Al/~5 GPa and ~32% Al/~9 GPa, i.e. close to the binary trend at those compositions. The figure demonstrates a sharp maximum in work hardening rate near 29-30% Al and that about 0.1% B addition causes no consistent change in work hardening rate.

subfigures.description: Work hardening rate (GPa, 0-20) versus aluminium content (%, 0-42) for polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys. Filled circles joined by a solid line are labelled 'Binary Fe-Al'; two filled squares labelled 'Fe-Al-B' are indicated by dashed arrows. The binary data form a low plateau up to ~20% Al, a steep rise, a sharp maximum above the 15 GPa gridline near 30% Al, and a decline to ~5-6 GPa at 35-40% Al.

observations.observation: The panel is a single x-y scatter/line plot with ordinate 'Work Hardening Rate (GPa)' from 0 to 20 (ticks every 5 GPa) and abscissa 'Aluminium content (%)' from 0 to about 42 (ticks every 10%).
Two distinct data sets are marked: filled circles joined by a solid line labelled 'Binary Fe-Al', and two filled squares labelled 'Fe-Al-B' reached by dashed arrows.

The Binary Fe-Al curve stays below about 2 GPa up to ~20% Al, rises steeply between ~20% and 30% Al, reaches its highest single point just above the 15 GPa gridline close to the 30% Al tick, and then falls to roughly the 5-7 GPa level at 35-40% Al.

Individual circle markers at 20-29% Al scatter around the drawn joined line (e.g. points clearly above and below the trend line in that interval), so the solid curve is a guide to the trend rather than a fit through every point.
The two Fe-Al-B squares lie at approximately 20% Al / 5 GPa and 32% Al / 9 GPa, i.e. essentially on the binary Fe-Al trend at those compositions.
The figure title printed inside the plot reads 'WHR(1.5%-1%) - Al content', indicating the work hardening rate was measured over the 1.5% to 1% strain interval.
The caption states the work hardening rate was measured between 1 and 1.5% plastic strain for polycrystalline, as-cast or annealed Fe-Al alloys as a function of Al content.
The caption states the data are taken from Refs. [6,8] and the present study, and that two data points correspond to Fe-Al alloys containing about 0.1% B.
The citing text states the work hardening rate is low for disordered Fe-Al with less than 20% Al, rises to a sharp peak at 28-29% Al, and falls to a moderate value above about 35% Al.
The citing text states that very similar trends are seen over other strain ranges (0.5-1% or 1-2%) with the sharp peak always in the 26-29% Al range.
The citing text states that addition of B led to only a slight increase in flow stress with little consistent change in work hardening rate, as seen in this figure.
The citing text identifies the 28% Al alloy as the one corresponding to the peak in the work hardening curve of this figure.
No numeric value is printed at any data point; marker positions can only be read relative to the 5 GPa ordinate gridlines and the 10% Al abscissa ticks.
